publication.title: Prediction of Mechanical and Fracture Properties of Lightweight Polyurethane Composites using Machine Learning Methods

experiences.scope: Developed a full-stack machine learning workflow to model and predict mechanical and fracture properties of cenosphere-reinforced thermoset polyurethane composites — a complex low-data domain characterized by nonlinear material behavior.

data_experimental: Integrated multi-modal experimental datasets across 0–40% cenosphere volume fractions.
Engineered structured datasets capturing tensile/compressive modulus, tensile strength, specific strength, elongation at break, and fracture toughness.
Conducted exploratory data analysis (EDA) to quantify distributions, outliers, correlations, and nonlinearity.
ml_strategy: Expanded the dataset using statistical bootstrapping, synthetic sampling, and uncertainty-aware augmentation.
Developed, trained, and optimized shallow ANN and deep DNN models using TensorFlow/Keras.
Performed systematic hyperparameter tuning (architecture depth, activation functions, learning rate, batch size, regularization).
Applied feature scaling, normalization, and cross-validation to improve model generalization.
Achieved exceptional predictive performance (R² > 0.99, low RMSE) and demonstrated reliable extrapolation beyond the experimentally measured reinforcement range.
outcome: Showcased a scalable ML framework capable of replacing classical empirical formulations for material property estimation — accelerating materials design and innovation, especially in low-data environments.
